The expected final logits and layer traces were generated by a standalone
Python/NumPy scalar reference, not by Candle. The pinned environment was
Python `3.13.3` with NumPy `2.3.3`. The two-layer synthetic model uses token
positions `0..3`, sliding attention in layer 0, full attention in layer 1,
nonzero attention sinks, unequal top-2 routing weights, and packed expert
seeds `[1, 7]` and `[18, 26]`. Its synthetic E8M0 exponent is `123` so the
comparison remains informative at the existing `1e-4` tolerance across CPU
and CUDA.

The trace records attention, router selection, expert contribution,
post-attention hidden state, and post-MoE hidden state for token 4 at position
3. The Rust tests verify the raw fixture digest and compare the CPU reference,
CUDA executor, and independent values. This is a bounded synthetic receipt;
it is not a production checkpoint, tokenizer, exact-model parity claim, or
hidden download.
